facts.fact: UNICEF says it has supported MINEDUC for over five years to move the EMIS from paper to a fully digital web-based system, with the SDMS operational as a component of the envisioned digital EMIS.

systems.owner: MINEDUC with UNICEF and GPE support

facts.fact: A GPE blog by Educate! staff says Rwanda's School Data Management System houses the unique ID number of every teacher and all the nation's students, almost 4 million.

note: Health records document; nothing on education.

systems.owner: National Examination and School Inspection Authority

note: CAMIS is an assessment system of the examinations authority, not the ministry's EMIS.
States no EMIS for Rwanda; the EMIS pilot was in Mauritius.

facts.fact: The Harvard CAS field report says Rwanda's Ministry of Education runs the web-based SDMS, with which annual education statistics are now compiled in a fraction of the time.
The report says, from a headteacher, that every student is assigned a unique ID in the SDMS, which tracks enrolment and attendance per student, with school compliance up from 40% to 70-80%.
The report says, from a headteacher, that the SDMS integrates with the national identity system, though it does not yet fully connect with other management systems.

note: The EMIS is named only as an integration target; no census or learner record is stated.
Cites 2017 education statistics only; no education information system stated.
